- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% to align with true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 2–3% below peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 period lag in true trend reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 period horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 5–7 periods if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
